labels: Viral RNA is introduced into cell
Viral DNA is produced by reverse transcriptase
Viral DNA incorporates into host genome
New viral RNA is produced by the infected cell
New viruses can infect other cells
NOTE: Infected cell can survive while viruses are being replicated and released
note: Caption 'Figure 7.6 Replication of retrovirus' lies below target_box_in_crop (own block), so it is excluded; running header 'HUMAN HEALTH AND DISEASE' and the body text below are also outside the box and excluded. This is a process flow diagram; labels are listed in the order the arrows run (virus with RNA core and protein coat -> infects animal cell through plasma membrane -> viral RNA enters cytoplasm -> reverse transcriptase makes viral DNA -> DNA joins host genome in nucleus -> new viral RNA -> new viruses -> released to infect other cells), with structural labels (Animal cell, Plasma membrane, Cytoplasm, Nucleus, DNA) placed where they first matter in that flow. A flat list loses which labels are process steps (arrow annotations) versus structure names, and loses that the released viruses restart the cycle in other cells. The NOTE line is printed inside the figure panel and is kept as the last entry.
